$comment: The Long Round — level packs. Schema in levels-schema.md. Seeds are CURATED: swept and certified by the Pack lab in course.html, not hand-picked. Wind is applied at runtime per hole (band/mph/from below); the certification is calm-air.

arc.title: The Long Round
arc.premise: The first disc ever thrown never landed. It is still riding the wind, and the wind it drags behind it is why nothing on this trail is ever calm. You arrive where it just passed. You always will.
arc.unlock: Pack N+1 requires pack N beaten. Holes unlock sequentially inside a pack, and a pack's back five opens once its front five has been finished once.
arc.beaten: Sum of every half's best <= target, so a ten-hole pack scores nothing until both halves have been finished once. Stars: 1 = finished, 2 = beat target, 3 = beat elite. Beaten packs unlock free replay of any hole.
arc.$comment: The trail has no last stop. `weeks` and `holesPerPack` are legacy cadence machinery kept for decode compatibility and read only by currentWeek, which gates nothing; every count comes from LevelsCatalog.totalHoles/packCount. Packs beyond the authored six are appended and unlock the same way.

worlds.title: The Long Round
worlds.subtitle: Six stops, and the story of them.

packs.title: Where It Lifted
packs.mechanic: Crosswind reading — the preview stops helping at medium, so aiming off becomes yours.
packs.intro: It left from here, they say. The grass under the old stand is still combed flat in one direction.

holes.name: First Light
holes.beat: The trail starts where the grass lies combed flat. A berm hides the pin; the wind wants your rise shot in the next county.
holes.certified: ideal 2/1 · 65m · standing→line · berm 8.4m

holes.name: The Bent Stand
holes.beat: Every pine on this hairpin leans the same way. Whatever came through wanted the straight line closed.
holes.certified: ideal 2/2 · 69m · drive→line · dogleg 0.85

holes.name: Understory
holes.beat: The collar around this pin grew in a season. Nothing gets in sideways any more — the only way is down.
holes.certified: ideal 3/2 · 76m · flop→flop→spike · 5-prop collar r8.1

holes.name: The Clearing Gale
holes.beat: It passed low over this meadow, and the air never settled. Straight into its wake, off the raised pad, everything you have.
holes.certified: ideal 3/3 · 179m · drive→spike→line

holes.name: Keeper of the Park
holes.beat: A ring of water where it touched down once — the only time it ever has. Land dead inside the ring, and you'll know how it felt.
holes.certified: ideal 2/1 · 33m · standing→flop · moat 7.1m wide

holes.name: The Combed Green
holes.beat: Past the old stand the grass turns with the path, all of it combed the same way. Follow the lean of it round — the straight line was never mown.
holes.certified: ideal 3/4 · 92m · standing→standing→line · dogleg 0.85

holes.name: Rainshadow
holes.beat: It rains on one side of this berm and never on the other. The pin keeps to the dry side, out of sight.
holes.certified: ideal 2/3 · 70m · standing→line · berm 9.1m

holes.name: The Old Stand
holes.beat: The oldest pines in the park closed ranks the day it left. Nothing gets in under the boughs any more — over the top is all they allow.
holes.certified: ideal 3/4 · 63m · line→flop→spike · 7-prop collar r8.2

holes.name: Night Gale
holes.beat: After dark the park empties and the wind comes back to practise. The long meadow, straight into it, with nothing to hold onto.
holes.certified: ideal 4/5 · 156m · drive→drive→line→drive

holes.name: Where It Rested
holes.beat: They say it set down on this green once, for a moment, before the wind called it back. Rest yours where it couldn't.
holes.certified: ideal 2/3 · 39m · spike→flop · moat 7.2m wide

packs.$curation: Seeds selected by the Pack lab in course.html (sweep of 16 candidates per hole, demand 1.15, park pinned, brief forced). Gates: story-fit floors (bend dogleg ≥ 0.7, ridge berm ≥ 6m), finishable by the analyser, every brief check green, par as authored. certified = the ideal round the analyser found in calm air; pack wind will cost real players more. Sweep date: 2026-08-02.
packs.$tuning: Retuned 2026-08-02 from real play, twice: the author shot 10 against an authored 22, so the lines came down to 16/12 and then to 11/9 — two stars at 11 or better, three at 9 or better, against a pack par of 9. Star lines are tuned off what a person actually shoots, never off par: par-anchored lines are participation trophies. Pars are Frolfy's 1/2/3 scale (the design generator's 3/4/5 shifted down two), so packPar is informational rather than a target. Ten holes since 2026-08-11: front five frozen, back five from the design lab. packPar 18 (front 9 + back 9). Star lines design (front five identical).

packs.title: The Onshore Run
packs.mechanic: Crosswind shaping — every wind here comes off the sea sideways, and nothing reaches the pin on a straight line.
packs.intro: It went out over the water from this shore, and the water has been coming back ever since. Nothing here has grown straight in a hundred years.

holes.name: Trade Wind
holes.beat: The palms on this point all lean inland, and none of them grew that way. Whatever went through bent the shore before it bent the trees.
holes.certified: ideal 2/2 calm · 3 in 13mph · 73m · dogleg 0.90

holes.name: The Dune Line
holes.beat: A dune stood up overnight where the sand had lain flat for a century. The pin is somewhere on the far side of it.
holes.certified: ideal 2/1 calm · 2 in 16mph · 51m · berm 15.7m

holes.name: Sandbar
holes.beat: The tide left this bar standing and then thought better of it. Land dead on it — there is nowhere to run out to.
holes.certified: ideal 2/1 calm · 1 in 18mph · 27m · moat 7.6m wide

holes.name: The Long Shore
holes.beat: The whole beach, end to end, in the wind that came off the water behind it. Off the pad, and spare nothing.
holes.certified: ideal 2/3 calm · 2 in 24mph · 162m

holes.name: Round the Point
holes.beat: The last of the shore turns back on itself here. Shape it round the point, or spend the afternoon in the sea grass.
holes.certified: ideal 2/2 calm · 2 in 17mph · 82m · dogleg 0.90

holes.name: The Second Shore
holes.beat: Behind the beach there is another beach, older, that the sea gave up on. A dune stands across it that remembers the day it went out.
holes.certified: ideal 2/3 · 61m · standing→line · berm 8.0m

holes.name: Undertow
holes.beat: The water here pulls back before it takes. A bar of dry sand in the middle of the pull — land dead on it or go with the tide.
holes.certified: ideal 2/3 · 42m · spike→flop · moat 7.8m wide

holes.name: Sea Grass
holes.beat: The grass grew into the eddy it left going out, a ring with the pin at the bottom. Nothing gets in sideways — drop it through.
holes.certified: ideal 3/4 · 69m · flop→line→spike · 6-prop collar r7.9

holes.name: The Headland Gale
holes.beat: The last point before open water, and the gale comes round it sideways. Shape it round the head or lose it to the sea.
holes.certified: ideal 3/4 · 63m · standing→line→line · dogleg 0.90

holes.name: Out Past the Break
holes.beat: The longest run of sand on the shore, out past where the waves give up. Everything you have, and then the walk.
holes.certified: ideal 3/5 · 154m · drive→line→line

packs.$curation: Seeds selected by the SWIFT Pack lab (scripts/sweep-pack), not the browser one: 16 candidates per hole, demand 1.15, beach pinned, brief forced. Same gates as pack 1's JS sweep (story-fit floors — bend dogleg >= 0.7, ridge berm >= 6m; brief's feature present in the built terrain; finishable by the ideal player) plus one the JS lab cannot run — finishable under the AUTHORED WIND, not just in calm air. certified = what the Swift harness measured, so it is directly comparable to LevelPackTests' log rather than to pack 1's JS receipts. Sweep date: 2026-08-03.
packs.$tuning: Pars are set from the measured ideal, not the other way round: at par 2 every certified ridge candidate was an ideal-player ace, so the berm hole is a par 1. Every hole's ideal now sits at or above its par. Harness ideal for the pack is 10 calm / 10 under authored wind. Star lines are PROVISIONAL and want a real-play retune the way pack 1 got one — on pack 1 the author shot 2 under the harness ideal, and target/elite ended at ideal-1 / ideal-3. Extrapolated here to target 10 / elite 8. Shoot the pack, then set them from that. Ten holes since 2026-08-11: front five frozen, back five from the design lab. packPar 18 (front 9 + back 9). Star lines design (front five identical).

packs.title: Against the Grain
packs.mechanic: Downwind trouble — the wind gives you distance you did not ask for, and every pin here has something waiting long.
packs.intro: It came through low over the fields and the whole crop is still lying down behind it. The wind at your back is its wake, and it will take you further than you meant to go.

holes.name: The First Furrow
holes.beat: The first furrow points the way it went. A berm stands across it that was not ploughed there, and the hedge behind the pin is thicker than it looks from here.
holes.certified: ideal 3/2 calm · 2 in 14mph · 100m · berm 16.6m · 10 behind · 3 guarding

holes.name: Silo Corner
holes.beat: Everything the wind pulled off the fields ended up banked in this corner. Short of it is no good and through it is worse — you will have to come down on top.
holes.certified: ideal 3/1 calm · 3 in 17mph · 61m · 6-prop collar r6.7 · 5 behind · 8 guarding

holes.name: The Back Forty
holes.beat: The long field, with the wind square behind you. It will feel like a gift for about two seconds longer than it should.
holes.certified: ideal 2/3 calm · 2 in 20mph · 162m · 8 behind

holes.name: The Stock Pond
holes.beat: They watered the whole west field out of this pond and it has been standing ever since. The green sits in the middle of it, and the gale is behind you.
holes.certified: ideal 3/2 calm · 3 in 24mph · 70m · moat 6.8m wide · water 8m long · wet approach · 2 guarding

holes.name: The Turning Row
holes.beat: The rows turn at the fence line and so did it. The wind will happily carry you straight on into the ditch on the outside of the corner.
holes.certified: ideal 2/2 calm · 2 in 18mph · 88m · dogleg 0.80 · 10 behind · 5 guarding · wet approach

holes.name: The Gleaning
holes.beat: What the harvest missed, the wind banked into this corner. Come down on top of it — short is no good and through is worse.
holes.certified: ideal 2/3 · 57m · line→flop · 6-prop collar r8.2 · 3 behind · 7 guarding · wet approach

holes.name: Hedgerow
holes.beat: The hedge turned where it turned, and a hundred seasons thickened the corner. The wind will carry you straight on into it.
holes.certified: ideal 2/4 · 85m · drive→line · dogleg 0.80

holes.name: The Windmill
holes.beat: They built the mill to use the wind and the wind used it back — the mound it stands on wasn't there before. The pin is in its lee.
holes.certified: ideal 2/3 · 61m · standing→line · berm 8.1m

holes.name: The Flooded Acre
holes.beat: The gale behind you, the drowned field ahead. The green is the one dry acre left, and past it the water starts again.
holes.certified: ideal 3/4 · 74m · flop→spike→flop · moat 7.5m wide · water 8m long · wet approach

holes.name: The Last Load
holes.beat: The last field of the farm, the wind square behind, the barn doors open at the end. It will feel like a gift, and you know better now.
holes.certified: ideal 3/5 · 195m · drive→drive→line

packs.$curation: Re-authored 2026-08-03 after the first cut shipped and played easy. Swept by the Swift Pack lab (scripts/sweep-pack): 48 candidates per hole, demand 1.35, farm pinned, brief forced. Gates: the brief's feature present in the built terrain, the hairpin floor raised 0.70 -> 0.80 (farm's dogleg ceiling), finishable by the ideal player in calm air AND under the authored wind, and — new — every hole DEFENDED both ways: trouble past the pin (water, or cover standing in the 2-26m band behind it) and trouble short (water on the approach, or >= 3 blocking props over the last 45m). The bomber is a documented exception: that brief clears its own corridor, so it had 0 guarding props on all 48 candidates every sweep, and is gated on long trouble alone at a higher bar. Certification rates under the defence gate: ridge 8/48, pocket 48/48, bomber 11/48, island 48/48, bend 2/48.
packs.$tuning: The first cut was built on the idea that a tailwind starves the disc of lift and lands it short. It does not — measured through the real model, a 24mph tailwind adds ~15m to a drive (109.7 -> 124.8) and doubles a flop (28.5 -> 57.7). So the pack handed out free distance and the holes had nothing to charge for it, which is exactly how it played. The wind still comes from behind on every hole; what changed is that overshooting now costs. Note what the sweep turned up while gating this: the oval platform puts its rim 30-39m past the pin on EVERY hole this generator makes, so out of bounds never punishes an overthrow — long trouble has to be water or cover. Harness ideal is 13 calm / 12 under the authored wind against a pack par of 10. Star lines are 9 / 7, set BY THE AUTHOR rather than extrapolated: they sit 4 and 6 under the harness ideal, where packs 1 and 2 sit at ideal-1 / ideal-3. That is deliberate and it is the tightest pack in the arc — note two stars is also the gate on pack 4, so if 9 proves out of reach the fix is to loosen it here rather than to grind. Ten holes since 2026-08-11: front five frozen, back five from the design lab. packPar 19 (front 10 + back 9). Star lines design (front five identical).

packs.title: The Narrows
packs.mechanic: Corridors — walls block from the ground up, and the funnelled wind comes back down them at you.
packs.intro: It came through at head height and every window on the block is still ringing. The wind it dragged in has nowhere to go but between the buildings, and between the buildings is where you are throwing.

holes.name: Off the Curb
holes.beat: Straight off the kerb and into it. The pin sits in a ring of planters and street furniture, and the wind is coming up the street to meet you.
holes.certified: ideal 3/2 calm · 3 in 14mph · 76m · 6-prop collar r6.4 · 5 behind · 7 guarding · wet approach

holes.name: The Service Ramp
holes.beat: The ramp banks up across the whole lane and the pin is somewhere behind it. Into this wind a rise shot stops being a rise shot about halfway up.
holes.certified: ideal 2/1 calm · 3 in 17mph · 55m · berm 15.1m · 7 behind · 5 guarding

holes.name: The Avenue
holes.beat: Four blocks of it, and it turns hard at the end. The wind funnels the whole length square in your face — you will not get there in one, and it will let you believe you might.
holes.certified: ideal 2/3 calm · 2 in 20mph · 133m · dogleg 1.20 · 5 behind · 5 guarding

holes.name: The Flooded Lot
holes.beat: The lot flooded years ago and nobody drained it. What is left standing in the middle is the green, the gale is straight down the throat of it, and there is water waiting eight metres past the pin.
holes.certified: ideal 2/2 calm · 4 in 24mph · 57m · moat 7.6m wide · water 8m long · 7 behind · 6 guarding · wet approach

holes.name: Hairpin Alley
holes.beat: It doubles back on itself between two walls. This one is not into the wind — it is across it, and the gust comes out of the side street at exactly the wrong moment.
holes.certified: ideal 2/1 calm · 2 in 18mph · 59m · dogleg 1.10 · 5 behind · 11 guarding

holes.name: The Underpass
holes.beat: Where the road dips under the rail line, everything the wind carries collects. The pin sits in a ring of what it dropped — come down through the gap.
holes.certified: ideal 3/4 · 51m · line→line→flop · 7-prop collar r8.1 · 3 behind · 7 guarding · wet approach

holes.name: The Retaining Wall
holes.beat: They poured this wall to hold the hill back, and it holds the wind instead. The pin is tucked in behind it, out of the funnel.
holes.certified: ideal 2/3 · 40m · standing→line · berm 5.5m · 3 guarding

holes.name: The Second Mile
holes.beat: The avenue keeps going after the streetlights give up. Straight down it, into the same wind as always.
holes.certified: ideal 3/5 · 145m · drive→line→line

holes.name: Crosstown Gale
holes.beat: Once a year the wind forgets which street it lives on and takes the cross street instead. Today. The corner is walled — go round the way it went.
holes.certified: ideal 2/4 · 86m · drive→line · dogleg 1.20 · 6 guarding

holes.name: The Reservoir
holes.beat: The city keeps its water up here, flat and black and patient. The platform in the middle is the green, and the city keeps what misses.
holes.certified: ideal 2/3 · 35m · spike→flop · moat 5.9m wide · water 8m long · 3 guarding · wet approach

packs.$curation: Swept by the Swift Pack lab (scripts/sweep-pack): 48 candidates per hole, demand 1.35, city pinned, brief forced, every hole certified finishable by the ideal player in calm air AND under its authored wind, and DEFENDED both ways. Certification rates: pocket 48/48, ridge 25/48, bend par 3 14/48, island 48/48, bend par 1 17/48. NO BOMBER, and that is structural rather than a preference: city certified 2/48 on that brief and 0/48 at par 3, because the bomber's job is to clear a corridor and this scenery's entire defence is the corridor. The long hole is a long bend instead. Sweep date: 2026-08-04.
packs.$tuning: The wind is the headwind, and it is measured rather than assumed — scripts/sweep-pack's `wind` probe puts the ideal player at 2.33 strokes into it against 1.98 with it in this scenery, with a left-hand crosswind at 2.35, which is why hole 5 turns across the gust instead of into it. Harness ideal is 11 calm / 14 under the authored wind against a pack par of 9. Star lines 10/8 are PROVISIONAL and sit at ideal−1 / ideal−3, the shape packs 1 and 2 shipped at, because nobody has played this pack yet: pack 3's tighter 9/7 was set by an author who had. Retune from real play, and note two stars here is the gate on pack 5 — if 10 proves out of reach the fix is to loosen it, not to grind. Ten holes since 2026-08-11: front five frozen, back five from the design lab. packPar 18 (front 9 + back 9). Star lines re-derived: our par 18 + design margin 5/1. PROVISIONAL — the back five has not been swept against this front five; re-run scripts/sweep-pack and retune before treating these as certified.

packs.title: Shallow Water
packs.mechanic: The flop — short holes walled in coral, and a crossing current that taxes anything you leave hanging.
packs.intro: It went out over the water and it did not come down. The shelf below is where the sea kept the sound of it, and down here the current does the work the wind used to.

holes.name: The Shallows
holes.beat: The shelf comes up almost to the surface here and the pin sits in a bowl of it. Fifteen heads of coral stand behind the basket — running the disc out is not a miss you get back.
holes.certified: ideal 2/2 calm · 2 in 13mph · 72m · 6-prop collar r7.1 · 15 behind · 10 guarding

holes.name: Fan Wall
holes.beat: A wall of fan coral stands across the whole line and the pin is behind it. Short and blind, so the shot is all height — and height is exactly what the current is charging for.
holes.certified: ideal 1/1 calm · 2 in 17mph · 39m · berm 18.6m · 23 behind · 9 guarding

holes.name: The Blue Hole
holes.beat: The shelf just stops. What is left is a pillar of coral with the basket on it and the trench going down all the way round, and the current across it is at its worst.
holes.certified: ideal 2/1 calm · 2 in 24mph · 31m · moat 5.6m wide · water 9m long · 16 behind · 10 guarding · wet approach

holes.name: Staghorn Gap
holes.beat: A gap in the staghorn, and it bends the moment you are through it. Sixteen heads guard the last stretch and the current is pushing you into every one of them.
holes.certified: ideal 2/1 calm · 3 in 18mph · 40m · dogleg 0.85 · 15 behind · 16 guarding

holes.name: The Long Shelf
holes.beat: The long run out along the edge of the shelf, curving the whole way. It is the one hole down here with room to throw, and the current has the whole flight to work on you.
holes.certified: ideal 2/2 calm · 2 in 20mph · 109m · dogleg 1.10 · 6 behind · 3 guarding

holes.name: Low Tide
holes.beat: Twice a day the sea steps back and the reef stands up. A crest of coral across the line, bare and drying — the pin is behind it, for now.
holes.certified: ideal 2/3 · 58m · standing→line · berm 7.6m · 3 guarding

holes.name: The Nursery
holes.beat: The young coral grows in a closed ring, tended by the eddy it left. Nothing gets in sideways here either — down through the middle.
holes.certified: ideal 3/4 · 62m · line→line→flop · 6-prop collar r6.7 · 3 behind · 5 guarding

holes.name: Second Shelf
holes.beat: Past the first drop there is another shelf, longer, with nothing on it. The whole length of it, and hold your line.
holes.certified: ideal 5/5 · 137m · drive→line→drive→line→line

holes.name: The Gale Across the Flats
holes.beat: The flats hold an inch of water and the gale holds everything else. One dry stand in the middle — only what lands dead stays dry.
holes.certified: ideal 2/3 · 53m · spike→flop · moat 6.7m wide · water 8m long · 3 guarding · wet approach

holes.name: The Channel
holes.beat: The deep channel bends round the last of the reef, and the reef leans over it. Shape it round — the straight line is under water.
holes.certified: ideal 3/4 · 83m · drive→line→line · dogleg 0.75 · 3 guarding

packs.$curation: Swept by the Swift Pack lab (scripts/sweep-pack): 48 candidates per hole, demand 1.35, reef pinned, brief forced, certified in calm air AND under the authored wind, and DEFENDED both ways. Certification rates: pocket 46/48, ridge 27/48, island 48/48, bend par 1 14/48, bend par 2 18/48. Hole 3 was authored par 2 and re-swept as a par 1: all 48 certified candidates at par 2 were an ideal-player ace, so the par carried no information — the same tell that made pack 2's ridge a par 1 — and the par-1 brief deals a different, harder set of holes (ideal 2). Reef has NO LAKE (BiomeCatalog gives it lake 0.0...0.0, it being a submerged scenery), so the only water a reef hole can carve is an island's own moat; every other hole here is defended by coral, which reef has more of than any other scenery (55-100 props). Sweep date: 2026-08-04.
packs.$tuning: The stub sold this pack as "water everywhere", and reef cannot deal that — see the curation note. The mechanic is the other half of what the stub said, the flop, and the current is a CROSSING one because that is what actually costs here: scripts/sweep-pack's `wind` probe puts the ideal player at 1.90/2.04 across the line against 1.42/1.46 along it, the opposite of the arc's assumption that the headwind is always the punishing direction. These holes are short, so drift beats carry. Pack 2 is nominally the crosswind pack but is asking a different question — aim-off on a long bend, against hang time on a short drop, and a flop is the shot that hangs. Harness ideal is 9 calm / 11 under the authored wind against a pack par of 7. Star lines 8/6 are PROVISIONAL at ideal−1 / ideal−3, same reasoning as pack 4: unplayed content gets the pack 1/2 shape, not pack 3's author-tightened one. Ten holes since 2026-08-11: front five frozen, back five from the design lab. packPar 16 (front 7 + back 9). Star lines re-derived: our par 16 + design margin 10/6. PROVISIONAL — the back five has not been swept against this front five; re-run scripts/sweep-pack and retune before treating these as certified.

packs.title: Under It At Last
packs.mechanic: Everything, one brief each — and the mountain charges across the line, not into it.
packs.intro: It has been circling the mountain, riding the heat off the caldera. Tonight it comes low enough to touch — and touching it is not catching it. Every wind up here is the wind it drags round behind it, and it comes at you sideways. When it lifts off the ridge it keeps climbing, and the trail climbs after it.

holes.name: The Cinder Road
holes.beat: The old road up the mountain switches back where the flow cut it. It went around — nothing that tried to go straight is still standing, and eleven of them are still in your way.
holes.certified: ideal 3/2 calm · 2 in 17mph · 99m · dogleg 0.90 · 5 behind · 11 guarding

holes.name: The Fumarole
holes.beat: A collar of rock grew around the one vent that never stopped breathing. Nothing gets in sideways, and sideways is the only thing the wind is offering — drop yours down the throat.
holes.certified: ideal 2/2 calm · 2 in 19mph · 77m · 6-prop collar r7.0 · 9 behind · 7 guarding

holes.name: The Ash Wall
holes.beat: The last eruption threw up a wall of ash nineteen metres high and the wind has been sharpening it ever since. The pin sits in its lee, out of sight until you have already committed.
holes.certified: ideal 2/1 calm · 2 in 21mph · 49m · berm 19.2m · 10 behind · 9 guarding

holes.name: The Caldera Run
holes.beat: The long straight over the shoulder of the mountain, into the heat and the gale riding round it. It flies this line every night. Tonight you fly it too, and the gale is across you the whole way.
holes.certified: ideal 2/2 calm · 2 in 24mph · 137m · 6 behind · 3 guarding

holes.name: Under It At Last
holes.beat: A green in a ring of lava, dead under where it circles. Nine metres past the pin the ground stops being ground. Put your disc down where it never has — and then look up.
holes.certified: ideal 2/2 calm · 2 in 24mph · 50m · moat 5.6m wide · lava 9m long · 6 behind · 10 guarding · wet approach

holes.name: After It Touched
holes.beat: It touched, and it lifted, and the mountain is still ringing. A collar of rock around the place — drop yours where the ringing is loudest.
holes.certified: ideal 3/4 · 78m · flop→flop→flop · 6-prop collar r6.5 · 3 behind · lava 15m long · 4 guarding

holes.name: The Far Slope
holes.beat: The far side of the mountain, going down. The old flow turned here and the path turns with it; the wind comes across, as it always does up here.
holes.certified: ideal 2/4 · 75m · standing→line · dogleg 1.10 · lava 13m long · 3 guarding

holes.name: The Ashfall
holes.beat: The ash it kicked up coming down is still falling, in a wall that drifts and never lands. The pin is on the far side of the fall.
holes.certified: ideal 3/3 · 52m · standing→line→line · berm 6.9m · lava 15m long · 3 guarding

holes.name: The Descent Run
holes.beat: The long straight down the shoulder, the gale across you, the ground dropping away. It flew this line going up. You fly it going down.
holes.certified: ideal 3/5 · 190m · drive→drive→line · lava 7m long

holes.name: It Went Up
holes.beat: A ring of lava, and above it, nothing — this is where it stopped circling and went up. Put your disc down inside the ring and watch the sky.
holes.certified: ideal 3/4 · 53m · flop→flop→flop · moat 6.6m wide · lava 8m long · 3 guarding · wet approach

packs.$curation: Swept by the Swift Pack lab (scripts/sweep-pack p6): 48 candidates per hole, demand 1.35, volcano pinned, brief forced, certified in calm air AND under the authored wind, and DEFENDED both ways. The finale plays ALL FIVE briefs, one each. Certification rates: bend par 2 13/48, pocket par 2 47/48, ridge par 1 28/48, bomber par 2 4/48, island par 2 48/48. The bomber was authored par 3 and re-swept as a par 2: at par 3 exactly one candidate in 48 certified and the ideal player went round it in 2, the same no-information tell that dropped pack 2's ridge and pack 5's island a rung. Volcano is the hardest scenery in the arc to deal a bomber on (the scout certifies 1-4 of 32 at every par) because that brief clears a corridor and this mountain's defence is what stands in it; the winner is the only one of the four that clears the general defended gate rather than the bomber's raised long-trouble exemption. No gate was softened for this pack: volcano clears pack 3's defended gate on its own props (10-26 blockers guard a typical approach) and pack 3's story-fit floors untouched (dogleg 0.80-0.95, berms 16-19m). The moat and the dealt lake are both LAVA here (the scenery-coherence pass), so 'wet' in these receipts is the mountain's own hazard. Sweep date: 2026-08-05.
packs.$tuning: WINDS ARE CROSSWINDS, and that is a measurement rather than a mood. The design project authored the finale as a dead headwind from 0 degrees — the thing overhead comes low and you throw straight into it — and scripts/sweep-pack's `wind` probe puts the ideal player at 1.58 into a volcano headwind and 1.54 with it, against 2.06 across the line either way. This mountain is reef's shape, not city's. So the bearings march round the compass (224 -> 262 -> 288 -> 66 -> 96) because the thing is circling, and every one of them sits on or near a cross axis because that is where volcano actually charges. That is the third time the arc has assumed a wind direction and been wrong; the probe is cheaper than the re-author. TWO GALES — the bomber set piece and hole 30 itself — are the one deliberate break of the arc's one-gale rule, and this is the pack that gets to break it. Harness ideal is 11 calm / 10 under the authored wind against a pack par of 9. Star lines 11 / 9 are PROVISIONAL at target = calm ideal, elite = ideal-2 — packs 2 and 4's shape for unplayed content, not pack 3's author-tightened one. If the finale proves cruel, loosen target before softening the winds: the winds are the only thing here that was measured. Ten holes since 2026-08-11: front five frozen, back five from the design lab. packPar 19 (front 9 + back 10). Star lines design (front five identical).

packs.title: Into the Teeth
packs.mechanic: Into the wind — every hole is thrown into the face of it, so the disc stops short of the line the arc draws and the answer is a rung up the ladder rather than an aim-off.
packs.intro: It went north, and the wind that carries it turned to meet you. There is nothing on this shelf to break it: no trees, no walls, four hundred miles of open ice and then here. The arc on the ground still draws the still-air line and the air has not been still since you arrived. It is out ahead of the weather, the way it always is.

holes.name: First Light
holes.beat: Dawn comes flat along the ice, all glare and no warmth in it. The way round bends hard where the floe buckled, and twenty-six blue shapes stand in the turn with the light behind them.
holes.certified: ideal 3/2 calm · 4 in 13mph · 78m · dogleg 0.85 · 3 behind · 26 guarding

holes.name: The Lee Side
holes.beat: One patch of still air on the whole shelf, and the basket is sitting in the middle of it inside a ring of six leaning stones. Everything outside the ring is still moving.
holes.certified: ideal 3/1 calm · 2 in 14mph · 36m · 6-prop collar r7.3 · 5 behind · 17 guarding

holes.name: The Long Fetch
holes.beat: Nothing has stood between this wind and here for four hundred miles. It comes up the face of a fifteen-metre drift and over the top of it, gathering the whole way.
holes.certified: ideal 2/2 calm · 3 in 16mph · 60m · berm 15.1m · 7 behind · 22 guarding

holes.name: The Lead
holes.beat: A lead has opened in the ice and the water in it is black and flat and six metres across. The wind will not let anything cross it high.
holes.certified: ideal 2/2 calm · 2 in 17mph · 59m · moat 5.9m wide · 6 behind · water 8m long · 6 guarding · wet approach

holes.name: Whiteout
holes.beat: The air fills with lifted snow and the horizon goes with it. The trail is still there underneath, still turning, and something ahead of the turn is still moving away.
holes.certified: ideal 2/2 calm · 4 in 22mph · 103m · dogleg 0.85 · 3 behind · 22 guarding

holes.name: The Drift
holes.beat: A drift twenty metres deep built itself across the line overnight, smooth on this side and cut away on the other. It was not here yesterday.
holes.certified: ideal 2/1 calm · 2 in 15mph · 63m · berm 19.5m · 6 behind · 9 guarding

holes.name: The Hollow
holes.beat: A dip in the shelf where meltwater stood and froze rough. The wind goes over the top of the hollow and the hollow keeps its own weather, which is worse.
holes.certified: ideal 3/2 calm · 2 in 19mph · 60m · 6-prop collar r6.9 · 5 behind · 14 guarding · wet approach

holes.name: Quartering
holes.beat: It comes off the left shoulder now, quartering, and the snow it carries crosses the line instead of running down it. The hairpin here was cut by this same wind, years of it.
holes.certified: ideal 1/2 calm · 2 in 21mph · 78m · dogleg 0.90 · 3 behind · 21 guarding

holes.name: The Second Lead
holes.beat: Another lead, wider, and the far side is a shelf barely bigger than the basket standing on it. Nine shapes wait past the water for anything that carries too far.
holes.certified: ideal 2/2 calm · 2 in 18mph · 48m · moat 6.8m wide · 9 behind · water 9m long · 8 guarding · wet approach

holes.name: Into It
holes.beat: Straight into the teeth of it, a hundred and eighteen metres with a ridge of ice standing in the middle of them. The gale comes off the pole with nothing in between, and what it is chasing is still out ahead of it.
holes.certified: ideal 2/3 calm · 2 in 26mph · 118m · berm 16.3m · 5 behind · 3 guarding

packs.$curation: Swept by the Swift Pack lab (scripts/sweep-pack --spec, the first pack authored through frolf-levels-pack): 48 candidates per hole, demand 1.35, arctic pinned, brief forced, certified in calm air AND under the authored wind, and DEFENDED both ways. Certification rates: bend par 2 6/48, pocket par 1 45/48, ridge par 2 8/48, island par 2 48/48, bend par 2 10/48, ridge par 1 26/48, pocket par 2 43/48, bend par 2 5/48, island par 2 48/48, ridge par 3 8/48. NO BOMBER, and that is the sweep's finding rather than a preference: three bomber holes were specced and every one certified 3-4 of 48 with the winner coming back `0 guarding`, 44-45 of 48 rejections being undefended holes. That brief clears a corridor and open arctic ground has nothing else to defend with, so the corridor was the only defence there could have been. Raising demand to 1.5 changed none of it. Same shape as pack 4's no-bomber note for city, arrived at independently. Hole 5 was authored par 3 and re-swept as a par 2: at par 3 the ideal player went round it in 2 calm and 1 windy, the same no-information tell that dropped pack 2's ridge and pack 5's island a rung. At par 2 it is 103m, 22 guarding, and the wind costs two strokes. No gate was softened. Sweep date: 2026-08-13.
packs.$tuning: THE WIND IS A HEADWIND, and that is the pack. Every bearing sits within 20 degrees of 0 — the thing overhead went north and the wind it drags is coming back down the line at you — which makes this the first stop on the trail that tests the loft ladder rather than aim-off. Packs 1 and 2 are crosswind reading and shaping, pack 3 is downwind trouble; into it was the one axis the introduction never asked about. STAR LINES ARE PROVISIONAL AND DELIBERATELY NOT PACK 6's SHAPE. Harness ideal is 22 calm and 25 under the authored wind, against a pack par of 19 — the first pack where the authored wind costs MORE than the calm ideal by a clear margin (+3), which is the mechanic working. Setting target at the calm ideal the way pack 6 did would price the pack as if its own wind were not there, so target follows the WINDY ideal (26 = windy ideal + 1) and elite sits at the calm ideal (22). If it proves cruel, loosen target before touching the winds: the winds are the only thing here that was measured. Every PlaytestHarness number is a floor — it has perfect knowledge of the flight model — so real play is harder than these lines assume, never easier. ONE GALE, on the long hole (10), per the arc's rule; pack 6's two-gale break is not inherited. Ten holes, front five and back five, packPar 19.
